title: The student years
hookLine: a student lies down in the mud to hold back the water; Hindu tradition calls it the student stage
tomorrow: a hero won his war, then wanted to quit. who talked him out of it?

lines: ARUNI LIES DOWN IN THE GAP.
cards: A first job, and someone older says: enjoy it, these are your learning years. Hindu tradition has a name for that season, brahmacharya, the student stage, and an old story to go with it.
A field, and a gap in the bank of a water channel. The teacher, Dhaumya, has sent his student Aruni to stop the leak. Aruni tries to bank it up with earth, and the water won't stop.
So he does the only thing left. He lies down in the gap and holds back the water with his own body.

teach.b: Evening comes. The teacher asks his other students: where is Aruni? Then he goes out to the field himself and calls: Aruni of Panchala, where are you?
Aruni gets up out of the mud and comes to stand before him.
The Mahabharata gives the teacher's answer: because you rose up out of the broken bank, you'll be called Uddalaka, and because you kept my word, all the Vedas will shine in you. Here's the teaching.
Hindu tradition names four stages of life, the ashramas, and the first is brahmacharya, the student stage. In the old picture, a student doesn't just take classes.
The student lives in the teacher's house, tends the cows and the fire, and learns by serving. Knowledge isn't downloaded; it's handed over, person to person, and the hand-off is earned by showing up.

teach.h: ONE DAY THE STUDENT GOES HOME.
teach.b: In some Hindu families, a thread ceremony, upanayana, still marks a child's start as a student. The story isn't asking anyone to lie in a ditch.

It's showing what the student stage is for: learning to give your whole self to what you were trusted with. Some things can't be learned from a page, only from beside someone, doing the work they gave you.
And the stage has an end. One day the student goes home, carrying the teacher's words into a life of his own, and the next season begins.

how: Hindu tradition describes four stages of life, the ashramas; the first, brahmacharya, is the student stage, pictured as life in a teacher's household. In some families the upanayana thread ceremony still marks its beginning.

he's right: a real student should get lessons only, never chores.

games.why: brahmacharya is lived in the teacher's house: tending the cows, the fire, the field. Aruni's lesson came through the task he was trusted with.

practice: Picture the student you were, at the start of your learning years. Say one line to them, quietly, out loud: one thing you've learned since, said kindly, the way a good teacher would say it.
Then rest a hand on your chest and stay with that younger self for the rest of the time.

wordCard.voice: The student years: brahmacharya, the first of the four Hindu stages, learning by serving a teacher. The seasons of life begin here.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the student stage, first of the four ashramas; the word is also used for self-restraint.

carryVoice: Keep this one: the student, and Aruni rising from the mud with the Vedas shining in him. Day 1681, the first season.
